1 │ # The edit helper crashes when I hand it a file path object
   2 │ 
   3 │ ## What happens now
   4 │ 
   5 │ When I pass a single file path object to the `edit` helper in Click, the program
   6 │ stops with a TypeError saying the path object is not iterable. That message says
   7 │ nothing about file names, so it gives me no clue what went wrong. If I wrap the
   8 │ same path object in a list first, the helper opens the file without any problem,
   9 │ so the failure only hits the single path case.
  10 │ 
  11 │ ## What should happen
  12 │ 
  13 │ I should be able to hand the `edit` helper a file path object, either on its own
  14 │ or inside a list, and have the file open in my editor exactly as it does when I
  15 │ pass plain text file names. The helper's own description should also say that
  16 │ path objects are accepted.
  17 │ 
  18 │ ## About this project
  19 │ 
  20 │ This project is Click, a Python library used to build command line programs. It
  21 │ provides the pieces a program needs — arguments, options, prompts, progress
  22 │ bars, and helpers such as opening a file in the user's text editor — without
  23 │ having to build them from scratch each time.
  24 │ 
  25 │ ## Problem this solves
  26 │ 
  27 │ I keep my file locations as path objects, not as text, so I would have to convert
  28 │ them to text by hand every time I want to open one in an editor. Having the
  29 │ helper accept path objects directly saves that conversion and removes a
  30 │ confusing crash from the middle of my program.
  31 │ 
  32 │ ## What changed
  33 │ 
  34 │ The `edit` helper now accepts file path objects as well as text file names,
  35 │ whether the path object is given alone or inside a list of files. The written
  36 │ description of the helper now mentions that path objects are accepted, and the
  37 │ release notes list this as a new thing in the unreleased 8.5.0 section. Nothing
  38 │ that worked before stops working.
  39 │ 
  40 │ ## Impact
  41 │ 
  42 │ Ease of use and correctness: one broken input now works.
  43 │ 
  44 │ ## User experience
  45 │ 
  46 │ Before: I call the edit helper with a single path object to a file, and the
  47 │ program stops with a TypeError about the path object not being iterable, with
  48 │ nothing about file names in the message. After: I call it the same way and the
  49 │ file opens in my editor, just as it does when I pass the same location as text.

content: **Plan

for the feedback report (to be written next round to `/megabit-feedback/round_1.md`)**

I read the ticket at `/megabit/ticket.md` and the staged diff (`
git diff --cached`, which showed `M CHANGES.md`, `M src/click/_termui_impl.py`, `M src/click/termui.py` plus untracked `.megabit_tmp/`). I also read `src/click/termui.py:838
-901` (the `edit` overload and body), `src/click/_termui_impl.py:710-742` (`Editor.edit_files`), `tests/test_termui.py:451-461` (`test_edit_pathlib`,

already in HEAD), `tests/typing/typing_edit.py`, `pyproject.toml:115-135`, and `.megabit_tmp/` listing.

**Findings the report should state**

1. The
product work the ticket asked for is present and looks right: `src/click/termui.py:901` widens the check to `isinstance(filename, (str, os.PathLike))` so
a single `Path` no longer falls through to the `Iterable` path; `src/click/_termui_impl.py:733` wraps a lone `str`/`PathLike` in a tuple; `src/click/_termui_impl.py:737` converts with
`os.fspath(name)` so a `Path` inside a list also works; the docstring at `termui.py:882-884` now says an `os.PathLike` may be given alone
or in a sequence, with a `.. versionchanged:: 8.5.0` block; and `CHANGES.md` gains an Unreleased entry referencing

issue 2869. Old string-only behaviour is preserved because the `os.fspath` conversion is a no-op for `str`.

2. The one concrete defect I can point
at is style/lint, not behaviour: `src/click/termui.py:841` and `src/click/termui.py:851` are both 91 characters, and every other line in the file is 87 or shorter (
measured with a small Python check, printed as `longest: [(87, 896), (91, 841), (91, 851)]`). `pyproject.toml:130` selects `"E"`
(pycodestyle error), which includes E501, so a ruff run in the harness's lint stage could fail on these two lines. This is the only

blocking item I intend to list, and it is a one-line-each mechanical wrap.

3. The test at `tests/test_termui.py:451
-461` is pre-existing (`git show HEAD:tests/test_termui.py` already contains `def test_edit_pathlib` at line 453), so the diff adds
no new test. The ticket itself did not ask for one, so I will not call that missing work — but I will note in
"Experience difference" that coverage of the new path comes from that existing test's `use_iterable` parametrisation (`single`

and `iterable` ids), which is adequate.

4. Not a defect, just observed: `.megabit_tmp/` is untracked scratch (leftover `editor-*.txt~
` and `pytest-of-megabit` directories from a run with a custom `TMPDIR`). Untracked, so it does not ship, and I

will mention it in one line at most.

5. Also verified as already correct, so the report will explicitly say it is
*not* missing: `tests/typing/typing_edit.py` already passes `Path("f.txt")` and `["f.txt", Path("g.txt")]` to `click.edit`, and `tests/typing` is in the my
py `include` list (`pyproject.toml:116`), so the widened annotations are type-checked. `import os` already exists at `src/click/_termui_impl.py:12`, and

`import os` was added to `src/click/termui.py` in the right isort position, satisfying the `"I"` rule with `force-single-line = true`.

**What must

be verified in the next call (harness runs the tests, not me)**

- The full `pytest` run: total count, pass/fail, and specifically
`test_edit_pathlib[single]` and `test_edit_pathlib[iterable]`, plus the existing `test_edit` and the `edit_files` argument-construction tests around `tests/test_termui.py:464
-480` (the `myeditor --wait --flag` and shell-metacharacter cases), to confirm the `os.fspath` change did not alter command

-line argument splitting.
- Whether a lint/format stage runs; if it does,

the two 91-char lines will be reported and should drive the verdict.
- The mypy `tests/typing` stage, to confirm the new `

str | os.PathLike[str] | cabc.Iterable[str | os.PathLike[str]] | None` annotation on both the overload at line 841 and the implementation at line 851 type-checks.

**Ver
dict I expect to recommend:** `approve` unless the harness's test or lint stage actually fails.
The behaviour the ticket describes works, the docs and changelog say what the ticket asked for, and nothing that
worked before is broken; the only thing I would ask for is wrapping the two over-long lines, which I will frame as a small non-blocking style
